title: Safran avvia i full-scale hybrid-electric demonstrator tests per la prossima generazione di ...
description:
Safran Aircraft Engines ha avviato una ground testing campaign presso il suo sito di Istres per il dimostratore PHILEAS.
PHILEAS è un full-scale engine demonstrato dotato di due electric machines dimensionate per l’impiego sulla prossima generazione di short- and medium-range aircraft engines.
Costituisce un passo fondamentale verso la loro integrazione nei nostri futuri motori aeronautici”, ha dichiarato Pierre Cottenceau, Vice President, Engineering, Research & Technology for Safran Aircraft Engines.
La progettazione delle apparecchiature elettriche è stata affidata a Safran Electrical & Power, il centro di eccellenza del Gruppo in questo settore.
Nel 2023, il DOPEE project ha validato con successo il funzionamento di una 300 kW electric machine progettata da Safran Electrical & Power e integrata nel Silvercrest engine.
text:
Safran Aircraft Engines ha avviato una ground testing campaign presso il suo sito di Istres per il dimostratore PHILEAS.

“Supportato dalla French Civil Aviation Authority (DGAC), il programma mira ad accelerare la maturazione delle hybrid-electric technologies per la prossima generazione di motori aeronautici. La hybrid-electric propulsion è uno dei tre pilastri della strategia di decarbonizzazione di Safran, insieme ad architetture innovative come l’Open Fan e all’introduzione di sustainable aviation fuel.

PHILEAS è un full-scale engine demonstrato dotato di due electric machines dimensionate per l’impiego sulla prossima generazione di short- and medium-range aircraft engines. Installati sugli alberi ad alta e bassa pressione, queste macchine possono funzionare sia come motori elettrici che come generatori. Il dimostratore integra anche onboard power electronics e electrical power distribution system. PHILEAS verrà utilizzato per validare l’integrazione fisica e funzionale di queste tecnologie all’interno del motore in condizioni rappresentative di operazioni reali. La campagna di test durerà circa sei mesi, per un totale di quasi 300 ore di prova”, afferma Safran.

“Siamo orgogliosi di avviare questa campagna di test a terra, che rappresenta un’ulteriore pietra miliare nella maturazione delle tecnologie ibride-elettriche. Costituisce un passo fondamentale verso la loro integrazione nei nostri futuri motori aeronautici”, ha dichiarato Pierre Cottenceau, Vice President, Engineering, Research & Technology for Safran Aircraft Engines.

“Condotta su uno dei Safran Aircraft Engines open-air test stand a Istres, la campagna è progettata per valutare la power extraction e l’immissione di potenza negli alberi ad alta e bassa pressione in diverse condizioni operative del motore e durante le varie fasi di volo. Il programma di test include scenari avanzati di gestione della potenza, come il bilanciamento della power extraction tra gli alberi ad alta e bassa pressione (power balancing), il trasferimento di potenza da un albero all’altro (power transfer) e la gestione degli scambi di potenza tra il motore e l’aeromobile (power sharing). L’integrazione di queste tecnologie mira a massimizzare la potenza elettrica disponibile per i sistemi dell’aeromobile, ottimizzando al contempo le prestazioni del motore in tutte le fasi del volo.

La PHILEAS test campaign è pienamente in linea con gli obiettivi tecnologici del programma CFM RISE, che si propone di ridurre le emissioni di CO2 del 20% rispetto ai motori attuali. La progettazione delle apparecchiature elettriche è stata affidata a Safran Electrical & Power, il centro di eccellenza del Gruppo in questo settore. Identificata da Safran come una soluzione promettente per la prossima generazione di motori aeronautici, la hybrid-electric propulsion richiede una stretta collaborazione tra gli esperti del Gruppo in electrical systems, engine control systems and engine integration”, prosegue Safran.

“Questa campagna di test si inserisce inoltre nell’ambiziosa roadmap tecnologica di Safran Aircraft Engines per lo sviluppo della hybrid-electric propulsion. Nel 2023, il DOPEE project ha validato con successo il funzionamento di una 300 kW electric machine progettata da Safran Electrical & Power e integrata nel Silvercrest engine. Durante tale programma, i team hanno effettuato i primi power extraction and injection tests su un high-pressure turbine shaft. Dalla fine del 2025, a Niort sono in corso anche test a livello di sistema su un test bench che simula un 800-volt aircraft electrical network”, conclude Safran.

(Ufficio Stampa Safran – Photo Credits: Safran)

title: Airbus and three French giants will turn farm waste into 160,000 metric tons of jet fuel, and it ...
description:
Europe is tightening its aviation fuel rules, while airlines are still struggling to find enough lower-carbon fuel at a workable price.
A fuel made from waste Rebound will use a technology known as Alcohol-to-Jet, or AtJ, to convert advanced ethanol into aviation fuel.
Why Dunkirk matters The Port of Dunkirk has already awarded Technip Energies an industrial site for the project.
The rulebook is tightening Under the European Union’s ReFuelEU Aviation regulation, fuel suppliers at EU airports must gradually increase the share of SAF in aviation fuel.
The International Air Transport Association (IATA) estimates global SAF production will reach about 2.6 million tons in 2026, equal to just 0.8% of aviation fuel use.
text:
Four French industrial giants are betting that part of aviation’s future may begin in fields and forests, not oil wells. Technip Energies, Airbus, Safran, and Tereos have agreed to create Rebound, a joint venture aimed at developing a major sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) plant at the Port of Dunkirk in northern France.

The planned output is about 176,000 tons of Alcohol-to-Jet SAF each year, which would make it one of the largest facilities of its kind in Europe.

The timing is not accidental. Europe is tightening its aviation fuel rules, while airlines are still struggling to find enough lower-carbon fuel at a workable price. In practical terms, this project is a test of whether Europe can turn climate policy into factories, supply chains, and fuel that actually reaches aircraft tanks.

A fuel made from waste

Rebound will use a technology known as Alcohol-to-Jet, or AtJ, to convert advanced ethanol into aviation fuel. The ethanol is expected to come from agricultural and forestry residues, which means the project is built around waste and byproducts rather than conventional food-based fuel crops.

Why does that matter to anyone boarding a plane for a vacation or a work trip? Because the fuel is designed as a “drop-in” option that can be blended with conventional jet fuel and used in existing aircraft engines and airport infrastructure. That is a big deal in an industry where airplanes stay in service for decades.

Hydrogen aircraft and electric flight still get plenty of attention, and they may matter later. For the most part, however, airlines need solutions that can fit into today’s fleets. That is where SAF has its strongest near-term appeal.

Why Dunkirk matters

The Port of Dunkirk has already awarded Technip Energies an industrial site for the project. According to the companies, that location should offer logistical advantages for moving feedstock in and shipping fuel out, while also helping with the permitting path.

That sounds technical, but it is central to the story. A SAF plant is not just a chemistry project in a lab. It needs trucks, ships, storage tanks, long-term contracts, and a steady flow of usable raw material.

Dunkirk also gives the project a broader strategic flavor. France is trying to connect agriculture, energy, and aerospace in one chain, and Europe is trying to reduce dependence on imported fossil fuels where it can. This is climate policy with an industrial hard hat on.

Four companies, one chain

Each partner brings a different piece of the puzzle. Technip Energies is acting as lead developer and engineering service provider, while Airbus and Safran join as industrial partners, offtake facilitators, and potential buyers of the fuel. Tereos, a French agricultural cooperative, is expected to supply and source the advanced ethanol.

That mix is important. Producing SAF at scale is not only about inventing a cleaner fuel, it is also about proving that farmers, processors, engineers, engine makers, aircraft manufacturers, and airlines can all make the economics work.

Technip Energies described the Alcohol-to-Jet pathway as a “credible, scalable route.” Airbus called Rebound a “vote of confidence in SAF.” Those are short statements, but they point to a much larger bet that cleaner aviation will depend on industrial coordination, not just good intentions.

The rulebook is tightening

Under the European Union’s ReFuelEU Aviation regulation, fuel suppliers at EU airports must gradually increase the share of SAF in aviation fuel. The mandate reaches 6% in 2030 and 70% in 2050, after starting at 2% in 2025.

That is where the pressure comes in. The International Air Transport Association (IATA) estimates global SAF production will reach about 2.6 million tons in 2026, equal to just 0.8% of aviation fuel use.

By comparison, Rebound’s planned annual capacity would equal roughly 7% of that 2026 global production estimate, although the French plant is still in development and would arrive later.

So, is this enough to solve aviation’s climate problem? Not by itself, but it shows the kind of scale the sector needs if SAF is going to move from press releases to regular airport supply.

The environmental promise and the catch

SAF is often described as one of aviation’s most practical tools for cutting emissions because it can reduce lifecycle carbon emissions compared with conventional jet fuel. IATA says SAF can typically cut lifecycle emissions by around 80%, depending on feedstock and production pathway.

Still, there is a catch. SAF is not magic, and it does not make flying emissions-free at the engine. The environmental benefit depends on the whole lifecycle, including how the feedstock is sourced, processed, transported, and certified.

That is why waste-based feedstocks matter so much. If the industry leans on materials that compete with food production or encourage land-use problems, the climate story gets weaker fast. The cleaner fuel chain has to stay clean all the way through.

What happens next

The Rebound joint venture is still subject to customary closing conditions and approvals, with finalization expected in the second half of 2026. The companies still need to choose the technology licensor, move through permitting, start pre-FEED and FEED engineering work, finalize feedstock and offtake agreements, and secure construction financing.

That may sound slow, but large energy projects usually move through gates for a reason. Each step reduces risk before partners commit to the next round of spending. No one wants a green megaproject that looks impressive on paper but cannot operate reliably.

At the end of the day, Rebound is less about one factory than about a new industrial model. If it works, farm and forestry residues from Europe could become part of the fuel supply for the next generation of aviation. That would be a real shift.

title: Egypt steps up as Africa, ME hub for sustainable aviation - Egyptian Gazette
description:
By Mohamed Attia Minister of Civil Aviation Sameh el-Hefny officially inaugurated workshop to launch the “Introduction to Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF)” project.

text:
By Mohamed Attia

Minister of Civil Aviation Sameh el-Hefny officially inaugurated workshop to launch the “Introduction to Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF)” project.

Organised by the ministry in co-operation with the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) and with support from the European Union, the workshop operates under the ACT-SAF programme.

This initiative represents a strategic milestone aimed at establishing a strong national SAF industry, helping Egypt diversify its energy sources, reduce carbon emissions, and meet global aviation standards.

During his opening speech, el-Hefny emphasised that hosting this workshop reflects Egypt’s growing standing within ICAO and demonstrates the international community’s confidence in the country’s ability to lead major regional green initiatives.

He noted that working closely with ICAO is a central pillar of the ministry’s strategy to transfer global expertise, build national capacities, and implement best practices.

This co-operation directly enhances the competitiveness and readiness of the Egyptian civil aviation sector to keep pace with rapid global changes.

The minister explained that launching this national feasibility study provides the crucial scientific and economic foundation needed to prepare a national roadmap under the CORSIA mechanism.

He stated that this programme represents an advanced model of international partnership based on knowledge sharing.

This effort directly supports the Egyptian state’s objectives of reducing carbon emissions, aligning with ICAO’s ambitious global target of achieving net-zero carbon emissions in international aviation by the year 2050.

El-Hefny outlined that Egypt possesses key natural advantages that qualify it to become a regional hub for SAF production.

These include its strategic geographic location, expanding green hydrogen and renewable energy projects, and modern aviation infrastructure.

He pointed out that the ministry has already implemented a comprehensive environmental programme through its updated National Action Plan.

This progress was recently highlighted by Cairo and Hurghada airports winning the Airports Council International (ACI) Environment and Sustainability Award, alongside Alexandria International Airport being honoured by ICAO Africa for its green infrastructure.

The opening of the workshop was attended by prominent international aviation figures, including Maria Gonzalez, ACT-SAF Project Coordinator at ICAO; Jacoba van Dijk, Technical Advisor for the project; and Farah Mesmar, representative of the International Air Transport Association (IATA), alongside other key delegates from ICAO and the European Union.

From the Egyptian side, key participants included Reem Orabi, Alternate Delegate of Egypt to ICAO, and Captain Karim Gamil, Advisor to the Chairman of the Civil Aviation Authority and National Focal Point for the ACT-SAF programme.

The Civil Aviation Authority was also represented by Captain Ahmed Sokkar, Vice Chairman for Airport Safety and Air Navigation; Pilot Mohamed Salah, Vice Chairman for Air Safety; and Ms Salma el-Tahhan, Head of the Central Administration for Air Transport. Pilot Ahmed Matar, Assistant Chairman of the Egyptian Holding Company for Airports and Air Navigation, also actively participated in the event.

The workshop featured extensive participation from various national ministries and research bodies, reflecting a unified domestic approach.

Key contributors included the Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources, the Ministry of Industry, the Ministry of Environment, the Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation, and the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities.

Specialised institutions also took part, including the Soil, Water and Environment Research Institute, the Egyptian Organisation for Standardisation and Quality, the Waste Management Regulatory Authority, and the General Authority for the Suez Canal Economic Zone.

Private sector and energy partners join the initiative

The event saw strong involvement from the financial, energy, and private sectors, including the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and the EgyptAir Holding Company. Energy and refining partners like Misr Petroleum, Assiut Oil Refining, Cairo Oil Refining, Amreya Oil Refining, and Nasr Petroleum participated alongside the National Authority for Waste Information and Data Management.

Private sector entities, including Qalaa Holdings, Icaro, Biodiesel Egypt, the Chamber of Travel and Tourism Companies, and the Egyptian Sustainable Aviation Fuel and Biofuel Company (ESAF), also joined to support the initiative. Following the workshop, ICAO and EU experts will continue working in Egypt for ten days to collect data and finalise the technical details of this national feasibility study.

text:
Lingkar.co Jelantah biasanya hanya jadi masalah, namun kini bisa mendatangkan rupiah ketika ditangani oleh Nawal Arafah Yasin melalui program Gerakan Minyak Jelantah Jadi Rupiah. Program untuk mendorong ekonomi sirkular berbasis rumah tangga itu diluncurkan Tim Penggerak PKK dan Posyandu di Wisma Perdamaian Kota Semarang, Jumat (17/7/2026).

Kegiatan yang selaras dengan program Gubernur Ahmad Luthfi dan Wakil Gubernur Taj Yasin Maimoen tersebut, diluncurkan dalam Kick Off Meeting Gerakan Minyak Jelantah Menjadi Rupiah,

Tampak hadir, Direktur PT BioSirkular Inovasi Indonesia Dicka Dwi Candra, Direktur PT Gapura Mas Lestari (GML) Rano Rusdiana, dan Pemimpin Wilayah PT Pegadaian (Persero) Kanwil XI Semarang M Aries Aviani.

Ketua TP PKK Jawa Tengah, Nawal Arafah Yasin mengatakan, gerakan ini menjadi langkah kolaboratif untuk mengubah limbah rumah tangga menjadi sumber daya yang bernilai ekonomi. Selain memberikan manfaat bagi lingkungan, program itu juga diharapkan mampu memperkuat perekonomian keluarga.

Menurutnya, masih banyak masyarakat yang menggunakan minyak goreng secara berulang hingga menghitam. Padahal, kebiasaan tersebut berpotensi menimbulkan berbagai gangguan kesehatan. Di sisi lain, pembuangan minyak jelantah secara sembarangan, juga dapat menyebabkan pencemaran serta mengganggu ekosistem lingkungan.

Berkaca dari kondisi tersebut, TP PKK Jawa Tengah menggandeng PT BioSirkular Inovasi Indonesia dan PT GML, untuk mengembangkan program pengelolaan minyak jelantah berbasis masyarakat.

Nawal menekankan, pengelolaan minyak jelantah menjadi sumber daya bernilai ekonomi membutuhkan kolaborasi multipihak, terutama keterlibatan keluarga sebagai aktor utama.

"Keberhasilan pengelolaan limbah minyak jelantah ini sangat bergantung sekali pada kesadaran dan partisipasi keluarga, terutama para ibu sebagai pengelola rumah tangga," tegasnya.

Melalui program ini, kader PKK di setiap desa dan kelurahan akan menjadi ujung tombak edukasi, sekaligus koordinator pengumpulan minyak jelantah. Gerakan ini nantinya juga diperluas melalui jaringan Posyandu yang jumlahnya mencapai 49.149 lembaga di Jawa Tengah.

"Bukan hanya PKK, nanti kita juga melibatkan Posyandu yang jumlahnya 49.149 lembaga. Ini merupakan potensi yang luar biasa untuk kita bisa membentuk ekonomi sirkular di Jawa Tengah," beber Nawal.

Menurutnya, konsep ekonomi sirkular menjadi sangat relevan, karena minyak jelantah tidak lagi dipandang sebagai limbah yang harus dibuang, melainkan sumber daya yang dapat dimanfaatkan kembali menjadi berbagai produk bernilai ekonomi.

"Bagaimana minyak jelantah ini juga menjadi sumber untuk diolah menjadi biodiesel misalnya, atau bioaftur maupun berbagai produk bernilai ekonomi lainnya," ungkap Ketua TP Posyandu Jateng tersebut.

Nawal menambahkan, saat ini minyak jelantah juga telah dimanfaatkan sebagai bahan baku pengembangan Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) di Kilang Pertamina Cilacap.

Pada kesempatan itu, pihaknya mengapresiasi TP PKK Kabupaten Batang yang lebih dahulu menerapkan program serupa. Dalam kurun waktu sekitar satu tahun sejak Juni 2025, program pengelolaan minyak jelantah di Batang mampu menghasilkan omzet hingga Rp170 juta.

"Ini membuktikan bahwa limbah rumah tangga kini telah menjadi bagian dari transisi, menuju energi yang lebih bersih dan berkelanjutan," imbuh istri Wakil Gubernur Jateng tersebut.

Sementara itu, Direktur PT BioSirkular Inovasi Indonesia Dicka Dwi Candra mengatakan, program tersebut merupakan tindak lanjut dari penandatanganan nota kesepahaman bersama TP PKK dan TP Posyandu Jateng, pada peringatan Hari Bumi, 22 April 2026 lalu.

Menurut Dicka, program dijalankan melalui empat aktivitas utama. Yakni edukasi masyarakat, penyediaan titik pengumpulan minyak jelantah di desa dan kelurahan, penjemputan oleh operator di tingkat kecamatan, serta pencatatan digital dan konversi hasil penjualan ke rekening masing-masing pengelola.

Dia menjelaskan, setiap satu liter minyak jelantah dihargai Rp7.000. Dari nilai tersebut, Rp5.000 diberikan kepada warga, sedangkan Rp2.000 masuk ke kas PKK desa. Proses konversi dilakukan melalui sistem digital, yang memungkinkan hasil penjualan dipantau secara transparan melalui aplikasi.

Selain memberikan tambahan penghasilan bagi masyarakat, program ini juga diharapkan mampu memperkuat peran kader PKK dan Posyandu, mendukung program lingkungan pemerintah daerah, serta menciptakan model pengelolaan limbah rumah tangga yang terukur dan berkelanjutan.

"Melalui program ini kita harap ekonomi sirkular berbasis rumah tangga akan aktif kembali dan menjadi penggerak untuk pembangunan keberlanjutan," kata Dicka.

Dalam kegiatan tersebut, TP PKK Jateng juga melakukan penandatanganan nota kesepakatan dengan PT Pegadaian (Persero) Kanwil XI Semarang, terkait sinergi program peningkatan pemberdayaan dan kesejahteraan keluarga, melalui gerakan pilah sampah menjadi tabungan emas. (*)

title: New 787 destined for Lufthansa to serve as ecoDemonstrator - Runway Girl
description:
A new Boeing 787 Dreamliner that is slated to be delivered to Lufthansa will first serve as Boeing’s newest ecoDemonstrator to flight test innovations that could improve fuel efficiency and reduce noise emissions.
These new procedures aim to curtail community noise around airports and identify opportunities for improving fuel efficiency.
First established in 2012, the ecoDemonstrator program advances the exploration of technologies that can help make aviation more efficient and sustainable.
In 2023, for example, sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) used in the ecoDemonstrator flight-test program was found to produce “dramatically” reduced soot particles and contrails.
We are pleased to support this year’s Boeing ecoDemonstrator Explorer program alongside Rolls-Royce,” says Lufthansa Group chief technology officer Grazia Vittadini of the carrier’s latest collaboration with Boeing.
text:
A new Boeing 787 Dreamliner that is slated to be delivered to Lufthansa will first serve as Boeing’s newest ecoDemonstrator to flight test innovations that could improve fuel efficiency and reduce noise emissions.

Powered by Rolls-Royce Trent 1000 engines, the 787-9 this month will begin testing a new reduced-length engine inlet with advanced acoustic treatments, in addition to new departure and arrival procedures.

The next-generation inlet “enables the integration of more fuel-efficient engines onto future platforms, and reduces weight and drag while maintaining the acoustic performance,” Boeing explains. Rolls-Royce provided engineering support and oversight for operating the modified Trent 1000 with the new inlet installed.

Also being explored are ‘Intelligent Operations’ flight paths, which are algorithmically generated using multiple data sources. These new procedures aim to curtail community noise around airports and identify opportunities for improving fuel efficiency.

The technologies being tested are part of Phase III of the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration’s CLEEN (Continuous Lower Energy, Emissions and Noise) program, a public-private partnership that sees government and aviation companies split the cost of researching and developing new green wing solutions.

First established in 2012, the ecoDemonstrator program advances the exploration of technologies that can help make aviation more efficient and sustainable. Through the years, Boeing has partnered with various airlines, including but not limited to Alaska Airlines, Etihad Airways, FedEx and United Airlines, and has evaluated more than 260 technologies, including more sustainable cabin interiors.

Their work has been quite meaningful. In 2023, for example, sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) used in the ecoDemonstrator flight-test program was found to produce “dramatically” reduced soot particles and contrails.

“Lufthansa Group and Boeing share a long-standing partnership in aviation. We are pleased to support this year’s Boeing ecoDemonstrator Explorer program alongside Rolls-Royce,” says Lufthansa Group chief technology officer Grazia Vittadini of the carrier’s latest collaboration with Boeing.

“Together, we aim to help advance aviation’s transformation by testing technologies with the potential to improve fuel efficiency, reduce noise and prove their value in real-world operations. ”

Testing begins later this month at the Boeing site in Glasgow, Montana, and is expected to run through mid-August.

text:
United Airlines stock sits at the intersection of robust travel demand and a complex cost backdrop as the carrier prepares for its next set of quarterly results. The Chicago based airline group United Airlines Holdings Inc. (ISIN US9100471096) has reported rising passenger revenue and growing loyalty program income over recent quarters, while investors watch closely how higher fares and premium offerings translate into sustainable margins in an environment of volatile fuel prices and ongoing labor cost pressure.

Revenue climbs with strong passenger demand

In its recent financial reporting, United Airlines has highlighted that total operating revenue increased compared with the prior year period, driven primarily by higher passenger revenue and additional income from its MileagePlus loyalty program. For example, in a recent quarter United disclosed that total revenue reached a level clearly above the same quarter a year earlier, supported by a double digit increase in passenger revenue and a notable contribution from other operating income such as credit card partnerships and ancillary fees. This improvement reflects continued recovery in international travel and sustained domestic demand, particularly on transatlantic and transpacific routes where yields have been higher than pre pandemic benchmarks.

The airline also noted that unit revenue metrics such as revenue per available seat mile rose versus the prior year, indicating that the company has been able to charge higher average fares or secure stronger mix toward premium cabins and preferred seating. In addition, corporate and high yield business travel has gradually returned, contributing to year over year gains in premium revenue. United’s management has emphasized that these dynamics, together with capacity discipline and a focus on profitable routes, have been central in driving revenue growth and improving the top line compared with the previous year.

Operating income improves against prior year

Alongside higher revenue, United Airlines has reported improved operating income relative to the same period in the prior year, even after accounting for elevated fuel and labor expenses. Operating margin expanded versus the comparable quarter, reflecting a combination of stronger yields, better load factors, and ongoing cost initiatives. In a recent quarter the company indicated that operating income rose by a meaningful amount year on year, and that adjusted operating margin came in above the level it had achieved in the equivalent quarter before. This was facilitated by higher capacity utilization, with available seat miles growing while maintaining or enhancing revenue per seat, and by optimization of its route network to focus on markets with stronger profitability.

Management has also pointed to nonfuel cost control as a factor in the improved operating performance. While salaries and wages have increased following new labor agreements and the need to retain and train staff, the airline has worked to offset these pressures through efficiency measures, better scheduling, and technology investments. As a result, the growth in nonfuel unit costs has been kept in check relative to revenue growth, supporting the expansion in operating income compared to the prior year period.

Earnings rebound compared with last year

United Airlines has reported that net income and earnings per share rebounded compared with the prior year quarter, moving from a lower profit base toward more normalized levels as demand recovered and international routes reopened more fully. In a recent quarter the carrier stated that diluted earnings per share were clearly ahead of the figure reported in the same quarter a year earlier, with adjusted earnings metrics similarly showing improvement versus prior year comparisons. This recovery in earnings has been attributed to the combination of higher revenue, improved load factors, and better pricing, together with the benefits of loyalty and co branded credit card revenue, which typically carries strong margins.

The company has emphasized that international long haul operations, especially transatlantic flights connecting the United States with major European hubs and transpacific services to Asia, have been key contributors to this earnings improvement. These routes often generate higher average fares and premium cabin utilization, which in turn help lift overall profitability relative to domestic operations. Management has indicated that demand in these markets is running above prior year levels, and in some cases above pre pandemic benchmarks, supporting a year over year increase in earnings.

Guidance signals cautious optimism

Looking ahead, United Airlines has provided guidance that suggests cautious optimism, with expectations for continued revenue growth and stable to improving margins, assuming demand remains resilient and fuel prices do not spike significantly. The company has indicated that it expects total revenue in upcoming quarters to be above the comparable prior year periods, driven by capacity growth in international markets and ongoing strength in premium and loyalty revenue. At the same time, United has acknowledged that cost inflation, particularly in labor and maintenance, as well as potential volatility in jet fuel prices, could weigh on margins, and has thus framed its outlook in measured terms.

United’s guidance typically includes projections for key metrics such as capacity growth in available seat miles, revenue per available seat mile trends, and adjusted operating margin ranges. These indicators provide investors with a quantified view of how the airline expects to balance growth and profitability. In recent guidance, the company has signaled that capacity will grow versus the prior year quarter, while unit revenue and margin are intended to remain at or slightly above the levels achieved previously, reflecting management’s strategy of focusing on profitable growth rather than simply chasing volume.

Balance sheet and debt profile

The financial position of United Airlines remains a central consideration for investors, given the capital intensive nature of the airline industry and the debt taken on during the pandemic period. United has reported total debt at levels higher than before the crisis, but it has also highlighted progress in reducing net debt through improved cash flow and selective debt repayment. In its recent filings the company has described a reduction in net debt compared with the prior year, supported by stronger operating cash flow and cautious capital expenditure planning. This trend is important for equity holders because lower leverage can reduce interest expense and financial risk over time.

United’s cash and liquidity position has continued to be robust, with available liquidity including cash, short term investments, and undrawn credit facilities comfortably exceeding near term obligations. The airline has emphasized that maintaining strong liquidity is a strategic priority, as it allows the company to manage periods of demand volatility, fund fleet investments, and service debt without undue strain. Over recent quarters, operating cash flow has been positive and improved relative to the prior year period, in line with higher earnings and better working capital management.

Fleet investments and capital expenditure

United Airlines is in the midst of a significant fleet modernization and expansion program, which has implications for both its cost structure and customer experience. The company has placed substantial aircraft orders with major manufacturers, including new narrowbody and widebody aircraft designed to improve fuel efficiency and offer enhanced cabin amenities. These investments, while capital intensive, are aimed at reducing unit fuel costs, improving reliability, and enabling growth in core markets such as long haul international and high density domestic routes.

Recent financial disclosures from United have indicated that capital expenditures have increased compared with the prior year, reflecting ongoing aircraft deliveries, retrofits, and investments in airport infrastructure and technology. Management has stated that these investments are expected to yield benefits over the medium term in the form of lower maintenance costs, improved fuel efficiency, and higher revenue potential from upgraded cabins and better on board connectivity. For investors, the pace and scale of capital expenditure relative to cash flow and debt reduction are key factors in assessing the long term risk and reward profile of United Airlines stock.

Fuel costs and hedging strategy

Jet fuel expense is one of the largest variable costs for United Airlines, and movements in crude oil prices can have a direct and significant impact on the company’s profitability. In recent quarters United has reported higher fuel costs compared with the prior year, as average fuel prices per gallon have risen from earlier levels. The airline has responded through fare adjustments, capacity planning, and operational measures to improve fuel efficiency, such as deploying newer aircraft and optimizing flight paths and speeds. These steps help mitigate the impact of fuel price volatility on margins, but they cannot fully eliminate the underlying cost pressure.

United’s hedging strategy has historically been more limited than some peers, with the company often preferring to manage fuel exposure through its broader commercial and operational strategy rather than extensive derivative hedging. As a result, United’s reported fuel expense tends to track relatively closely with market prices, making its earnings sensitive to swings in energy markets. Investors therefore pay close attention to management commentary on fuel price assumptions in guidance and its plans to offset potential increases through revenue management and cost initiatives.

Labor costs and workforce dynamics

Labor is another major cost component for United Airlines, encompassing pilots, cabin crew, ground staff, maintenance personnel, and administrative employees. In recent periods, United has negotiated new labor agreements reflecting higher wages and benefits, which have increased overall labor expense compared with the prior year. The company has indicated that these agreements are essential to retaining skilled staff, ensuring operational reliability, and meeting regulatory and safety requirements, even though they contribute to nonfuel cost inflation.

At the same time, United has worked to improve productivity and efficiency through scheduling optimization, training programs, and technology that supports workforce management. For example, enhanced crew management systems and predictive maintenance tools can reduce delays and cancellations, thereby limiting the need for costly overtime and disruption related expenses. The balance between fair compensation and efficiency gains is critical for sustaining margins, and United’s ability to manage this balance influences how investors view United Airlines stock.

MileagePlus and loyalty revenue growth

One of the most attractive assets within United Airlines’ business model is its MileagePlus loyalty program, which generates significant revenue through partnerships with credit card issuers, retailers, and other travel providers. In recent quarters, United has reported that loyalty and co branded credit card revenue has grown compared with the prior year period, contributing to a higher share of total revenue. This income is typically less cyclical than ticket sales and carries strong margins, providing a stabilizing effect on the company’s overall earnings profile.

The growth in MileagePlus revenue underscores the value of United’s customer base and its ability to monetize travel spending beyond the flight itself. As more customers enroll in the program and use co branded cards, United benefits from fees and revenue sharing arrangements that can rise steadily over time. For investors, the expansion of loyalty revenue is a key component of the investment case for United Airlines stock, as it diversifies the company’s income streams and supports margin resilience in periods when demand or pricing for core air travel may moderate.

Comparison with peers and industry context

When comparing United Airlines with other large US carriers, investors often look at metrics such as revenue growth, margin performance, leverage, and network strength. Recent industry data suggest that United’s revenue growth and margin recovery have been broadly comparable with peers, though differences in network focus and capital allocation strategies can lead to variations in performance. United’s strong presence in major hubs such as Chicago, Newark, and San Francisco, combined with extensive international routes, gives it a distinct profile compared with carriers that are more concentrated in domestic or regional markets.

United’s leverage remains higher than some competitors due to the debt taken on during the pandemic and the scale of its fleet investment program, which may be seen as a risk factor by more conservative investors. However, its improving cash flow and focus on debt reduction over time mitigate this concern to some extent. The airline industry as a whole continues to face challenges such as regulatory requirements, environmental pressures, and exposure to economic cycles, and United is no exception. Nonetheless, the company’s revenue and earnings recovery relative to the prior year provide evidence that United Airlines has been able to navigate these challenges while maintaining a competitive position in the market.

Environmental strategy and sustainability initiatives

United Airlines has publicly committed to various environmental and sustainability goals, including reducing its greenhouse gas emissions and investing in sustainable aviation fuel and more efficient aircraft. These initiatives, while only partially reflected in current financial metrics, have long term implications for cost structure and regulatory risk. United’s investments in new aircraft, operational efficiency, and partnerships related to sustainable aviation fuel are intended to lower emissions per passenger and per flight over time, aligning the company with evolving regulatory standards and customer preferences.

From an investor perspective, these sustainability efforts are relevant for assessing future capital expenditure requirements, potential carbon related costs, and the airline’s ability to meet increasingly stringent environmental regulations. United’s progress in these areas can influence its reputation and customer loyalty, which in turn may affect revenue and profitability. Although the immediate financial impact of sustainability initiatives may be modest, the longer term benefits in terms of reduced risk and potential competitive advantage are a factor in how some investors evaluate United Airlines stock.

Risk factors and volatility considerations

Investing in airlines involves a range of risk factors, and United Airlines is subject to many of them. These include macroeconomic conditions that influence travel demand, geopolitical events affecting international routes, regulatory changes, labor relations, fuel price volatility, and operational disruptions such as weather or technical issues. United’s management acknowledges these risks in its disclosures and emphasizes the importance of maintaining strong liquidity, diversified revenue streams, and flexible capacity management to navigate periods of turbulence.

Historically, airline stocks have exhibited significant price volatility, and United Airlines stock is no exception. Earnings can fluctuate markedly from quarter to quarter as demand, pricing, and costs move, and market sentiment toward the sector can change quickly in response to external events. For this reason, investors often look beyond a single quarter’s figures and focus on trends over several periods, such as year over year revenue and earnings growth, margin stability, and progress in reducing debt. United’s recent trajectory of improving revenue and earnings compared with the prior year, together with its investment in fleet and loyalty assets, forms the basis for many assessments of its medium term prospects.

Product and service focus across cabins

United Airlines offers a range of products and services across cabin classes, including United Polaris business class on long haul international flights, premium economy offerings, economy plus seating with extra legroom, and standard economy. The airline has invested in upgrading cabins, improving seats, enhancing in flight entertainment, and expanding Wi Fi connectivity, particularly on routes that carry higher proportions of business and premium leisure travelers. These product enhancements are designed to support higher yields and improved customer satisfaction, which in turn can contribute to revenue growth and margin improvements.

In addition to on board products, United has focused on its digital platforms and customer service, including mobile apps and website functionality that facilitate booking, check in, and management of MileagePlus accounts. The carrier’s customer experience strategy aims to differentiate its offering in competitive markets and build loyalty among frequent travelers. For investors, the linkage between product quality, customer satisfaction scores, and financial performance is an important consideration, as better products can support higher fares and repeat business, thereby reinforcing the revenue trends that underpin United Airlines stock.

United Airlines stock and market valuation

United Airlines stock trades primarily on the Nasdaq exchange under the symbol UAL, and its market valuation reflects investor expectations regarding future revenue, earnings, and cash flow. As of a recent trading day, the shares were priced at a level that implies a market capitalization in the multiple billions of USD, positioning United among the larger constituents of major US equity indices that include airline stocks. The share price has moved over time in response to quarterly results, guidance updates, macroeconomic news, and sector specific developments such as changes in fuel prices or regulatory announcements.

Equity analysts and market participants often compare United’s valuation metrics, such as price to earnings and enterprise value to EBITDA, with those of peers to assess whether the stock trades at a premium or discount to the sector based on its growth and risk profile. United’s improved earnings and cash flow compared with the prior year can support a case for valuation normalization after the disruptions of the pandemic period. However, the inherent cyclicality and risk in the airline business mean that investors usually maintain a degree of caution, and United Airlines stock remains sensitive to shifts in risk appetite and sector sentiment.

text:
A north Queensland cattle farming family is taking part in a trial growing oil-producing trees alongside livestock.

The Lawrie family, from Powlathanga station near Charters Towers in north Queensland, has been running a cattle breeding operation since 2004.

But now the family is taking part in a new venture.

In September last year, they turned a 10-hectare paddock into a renewable fuel trial, planting the oil-producing pongamia trees.

The trial is being completed with SilvoPlus, an entity of renewable fuel company JetZero Australia.

They're trying to determine the best way to run livestock alongside rows of pongamia, a legume tree with seeds containing oil that can be processed into biofuel.

Powlathanga grazier, Stephen Lawrie, said they wanted to take part in the trial to look at diversifying their income.

"You're always looking at different options, if something else interesting comes up that can work in conjunction with the cattle, I'm definitely interested in it," he said.

Ketti Ketmontri, the project lead for SilvoPlus, said the main purpose was to test the trees with grazing.

"We're looking at optimised grazing, how to produce fodder or cash crops in the interrow, and then when's the right time to bring sheep or cattle in," Mr Ketmontri said.

Trials across the country, nowhere to process

Pongamia trials have been breaking ground across Australia over the past decade, but there is currently nowhere that processes the oil into biofuel.

Ed Mason, CEO of JetZero Australia, has plans to build a biorefinery in Townsville that would take agricultural products and process them into sustainable aviation fuel (SAF).

"We're looking to take bioethanol and take about a hundred million litres of sustainable aviation fuel as well as renewable diesel," he said.

"That's a material volume for Townsville, enough to supply most of the airports in the region if we were to do that."

Demand for SAF is growing, with 38 countries now having a mandate for airlines to use it.

JetZero has completed road construction and land clearing at a 150ha site in Townsville, with the company expected to reach financial close at the end of this year.

"It would be two years of construction and we're trying to accelerate that and compress that as much as we can with our engineering contractors," said Mr Mason.

"First fuels will hopefully be coming by 2028."

A potential cattle feed source

Scientists are looking at the nutritional value of the outside shell of pongamia seeds to be used as cattle feed.

Associate Professor from the University of Queensland Sarah Meale has just finished a study feeding ground-up pongamia husk to cattle.

"The pongamia husks are the byproduct of that oil extraction. So, it's a very cheap feed source that is really quite high in protein. So up to around 20 to 30 per cent protein."

The trial included a zero, two and four per cent inclusion rate of the ground pongamia.

"Across all treatments, we have seen the exact same intake and the same growth rates, which is a really promising outcome."

"Right now, we know cottonseed is hard to find and very, very expensive along with other protein sources. This is the potential to replace those at a much lower cost."

Although the experiment had promising results, the lack of pongamia oil processing is a roadblock for the feed to be used more widespread.

"The scale at the moment is the problem. We don't have enough of the product to make it into the market."

Cattle to be priority

On Powlathanga, Stephen Lawrie remains interested in the future of pongamia, but wants cattle to remain the focus.

"Unless the trees could produce twice the amount of income as what the cattle could, we couldn't really consider it," he said.

"But if they can be run in conjunction, I think it's a win-win."

text:
Kinley Yangzom

Bhutan will serve as the primary research and certification hub for a pioneering international venture aimed at producing sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and biodegradable plastics from Pongamia trees.

The initiative, launched in Thimphu yesterday, establishes a strategic partnership between the Australian biotechnology company Ecopha and the Bhutanese company DrukBees Private Limited.

The project will focus on building a localised demonstration model in Bhutan before scaling the system up for larger global economies.

Speaking at the launch, Ecopha Chief Executive Officer and Co-founder Dr Wilson Ling said Bhutan’s renowned environmental leadership made it the ideal environment to prove the viability of a complete, replicable green system.

“We know that there is limited land and limited manpower in Bhutan, but we can make the whole system as a demonstration model and then show it to the world,” he said. “We show the result and the answer to everyone, and then countries like America, China, and India can follow accordingly.”

The core of the project relies on the cultivation of the Pongamia tree.

The non-edible seeds harvested from these trees produce an oil that can be processed directly into SAF, while the residual materials left over from refining will be utilised to manufacture biodegradable plastics.

Because Pongamia thrives on degraded land and does not compete with traditional food crops, the company considers the project a dual win for ecological restoration and renewable raw material production.

Rather than building a large industrial facility, the joint venture plans to start small by establishing precise Pongamia plantations and a localised biorefinery.

Nganglam has been identified as the preferred location for the initial plantation, with the first round of planting targeted for September.

Punakha is also currently being assessed for expansion following a recent site evaluation visit. The newly planted trees are expected to take approximately five years to mature before yielding seeds for processing.

To ensure strict compliance and product integrity, the company will deploy an advanced traceability system to digitally monitor every tree from planting to harvest. This system will record growth rates, geographic location, and environmental data, providing the foundational metrics needed to develop a global certification standard for all derived products.

Karma Dorji, promoter of Ecopha DrukBees Private Limited, said that Bhutan’s value in the partnership lies in intellectual and data-driven assets, rather than industrial volume.

“The mass production will happen in these big countries, but the model, certification, research and development, and the high-value work will happen in Bhutan because Bhutan is the right country to certify this product,” he said.

The company plans to spend the next five years maturing the complete research, tracking, and certification framework in Bhutan, establishing a blueprint that will eventually dictate the parameters for sustainable aviation products in much larger international markets.

text:
Ecobiz.asia – Indonesia and Japan have agreed to accelerate the implementation of Joint Crediting Mechanism (JCM) carbon projects while expanding cooperation on clean energy initiatives, including geothermal power, waste-to-energy, sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), green ammonia, and carbon market development.

The commitment was reaffirmed during a bilateral meeting between Indonesia’s Directorate General of New, Renewable Energy and Energy Conservation (EBTKE) under the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources and a delegation from Japan’s Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) in Jakarta on Wednesday (July 16, 2026).

Eniya Listiani Dewi, Director General of EBTKE, said the partnership is focused on accelerating strategic clean energy projects while strengthening investment in low-carbon technologies.

One of the priority areas discussed was the acceleration of two geothermal developments—Sarulla Geothermal Power Plant and Muaralaboh Geothermal Power Plant Unit 2.

“We are accelerating the development of the Sarulla and Muaralaboh Unit 2 geothermal projects. For Sarulla, the government continues to restore generation capacity through a three-phase Long-Term Restoration Plan while providing greater certainty for follow-on investment to optimize the plant’s capacity,” Eniya said.

She added that the Muaralaboh Unit 2 project is expected to increase the share of renewable energy in Indonesia’s power mix, strengthen the reliability of Sumatra’s electricity system, create jobs, increase the use of locally produced goods, and generate broader economic benefits.

Beyond geothermal energy, the two countries discussed several priority projects, including the Legok Nangka waste-to-energy plant in West Java, the Green Ammonia Initiative in Aceh (GAIA), sustainable aviation fuel development, small- and medium-scale nuclear power generation, and carbon market cooperation.

Indonesia and Japan also agreed to accelerate the implementation of the Joint Crediting Mechanism (JCM), including projects involving carbon capture and storage (CCS) and internationally recognized carbon trading mechanisms.

The JCM is a bilateral carbon crediting framework established by Japan to support the deployment of low-carbon technologies in partner countries while generating verified emission reductions that can be shared between participating governments.

On energy efficiency, Eniya said Indonesia continues to strengthen energy management in industrial facilities and commercial buildings through new regulations. As of 2025, hundreds of industrial facilities and buildings had submitted reports through the government’s Online Energy Management Reporting (POME) platform.

“These measures contribute to both energy savings and greenhouse gas emission reductions,” she said.

Eniya was accompanied by senior officials responsible for geothermal energy, energy conservation, and new energy development, while the Japanese delegation was led by Shinichi Kihara, Director General for Energy and Environmental Policy at Japan’s Agency for Natural Resources and Energy (ANRE).

This quantified comparison helps investors understand whether demand for renewable diesel and jet fuel is growing fast enough to offset any pressure in conventional refining margins or feedstock costs. It also shows how Neste is progressing in its strategy to increase the share of renewable products in its portfolio.

The valuation also reflects market expectations for the companys earnings from renewable fuels and traditional refining.

From a fundamental perspective, investors can compare Neste market capitalization with its revenue and profit figures from the latest annual report or interim period. A revenue figure in the billions of euros and an operating profit or comparable EBITDA number in the hundreds of millions of euros create ratios such as price-to-earnings or enterprise value-to-EBITDA, which help assess whether the stock is priced at a premium or discount to other energy and renewable fuel companies. The quantified comparison between current earnings and previous-year performance, combined with the current share price, underpins these valuation metrics.

Reporting on production volumes helps highlight the operational scale behind revenue figures and the potential for future growth as new capacity comes online. A comparison between current and previous-year production volumes provides another quantitative anchor for assessing the progress of Neste renewable business.

Oil products and other segments

The company also reports results in a Marketing and Services segment, covering downstream activities. Revenue and profit figures from this segment add to the overall picture of Neste earnings and provide another source of quantified comparison against previous periods. Together, the three main segments give investors a detailed view of how different parts of the business contribute to total revenue and profit.

Capital expenditure and growth investments

Neste has committed substantial capital expenditure to expand its renewable fuel capacity, including projects aimed at increasing production of sustainable aviation fuel and renewable diesel. In the latest annual report or interim period, the company disclosed capital expenditure in the hundreds of millions or billions of euros, with a clear breakdown between maintenance and growth investments. Comparing current-year capital expenditure with the prior year provides a quantitative measure of how aggressively Neste is investing in its transition strategy.

These quantified commitments help investors estimate future revenue and profit potential from expanded production. When combined with current earnings metrics and share price levels, capital expenditure data help inform long-term valuation and expectations for Neste stock.

Debt, cash flow, and dividend

In the latest reporting period, net debt stood in the billions of euros, and gearing represented a percentage of equity. The company also disclosed cash flow from operating activities, showing the cash generation capacity of its business. Comparing net debt, gearing, and cash flow figures with the prior year provides a quantified view of how its financial position is evolving as it invests in renewable capacity.

The company has a history of paying dividends, and its latest annual report set a dividend per share figure in euros. A comparison of the latest dividend per share with the prior years dividend shows whether payouts are rising, stable, or falling. This quantitative dividend comparison is relevant for income-focused investors, especially when viewed alongside earnings trends and share price performance.

Guidance and market expectations

In its recent investor communications, Neste has provided guidance for metrics such as comparable EBITDA or segment margins. This guidance often includes quantified ranges for the full year, reflecting managements view on market conditions for renewable and oil products. Investors can compare the guidance ranges with actual reported figures in prior years to assess whether the company expects growth or stability in earnings. This comparison creates a numeric link between current performance and future expectations.

Market expectations for Neste stock are also shaped by analyst estimates of revenue, earnings per share, and EBITDA. These consensus estimates, which draw on published forecasts, provide another quantitative reference point. Comparing reported results with consensus estimates reveals whether the company is beating or missing expectations and by how much in numeric terms. Such comparisons can be important drivers of short-term stock price reactions.

Representative renewable fuel products

Among its products, Neste is known for renewable diesel and sustainable aviation fuel, which are marketed to transportation and aviation customers aiming to reduce lifecycle emissions. Sales volumes and revenue from these products are reported within the Renewable Products segment. Quantitative data on volumes, average selling prices, and margin per unit help illustrate the economic contribution of these products. Comparing current volumes with previous-year volumes gives a sense of how quickly demand for low-carbon fuels is expanding.

text:
INDORAYA – Ketua Tim Penggerak (TP) PKK Provinsi Jawa Tengah, Nawal Arafah Yasin, meluncurkan Gerakan Minyak Jelantah Jadi Rupiah sebagai upaya mendorong ekonomi sirkular berbasis rumah tangga sekaligus meningkatkan kesadaran masyarakat terhadap kesehatan dan lingkungan.

Program tersebut diluncurkan dalam Kick Off Meeting Gerakan Minyak Jelantah Menjadi Rupiah di Wisma Perdamaian, Kota Semarang, Jumat (17/7/2026). Kegiatan itu turut dihadiri Direktur PT BioSirkular Inovasi Indonesia Dicka Dwi Candra, Direktur PT Gapura Mas Lestari (GML) Rano Rusdiana, serta Pemimpin Wilayah PT Pegadaian (Persero) Kanwil XI Semarang M Aries Aviani.

Nawal mengatakan, gerakan tersebut dirancang untuk mengubah limbah rumah tangga menjadi sumber daya yang memiliki nilai ekonomi, sekaligus mendukung program prioritas Gubernur Ahmad Luthfi dan Wakil Gubernur Taj Yasin Maimoen.

Menurutnya, persoalan minyak jelantah selama ini masih menjadi tantangan karena sebagian masyarakat masih menggunakan minyak goreng secara berulang hingga menghitam, yang berpotensi menimbulkan gangguan kesehatan. Selain itu, pembuangan minyak jelantah secara sembarangan juga dapat mencemari lingkungan.

Karena itu, TP PKK Jawa Tengah menggandeng PT BioSirkular Inovasi Indonesia dan PT GML untuk mengembangkan sistem pengelolaan minyak jelantah berbasis masyarakat.

Nawal menegaskan, keberhasilan program tersebut sangat bergantung pada keterlibatan keluarga, terutama para ibu rumah tangga.

“Keberhasilan pengelolaan limbah minyak jelantah ini sangat bergantung sekali pada kesadaran dan partisipasi keluarga, terutama para ibu sebagai pengelola rumah tangga,” tegasnya.

Dalam implementasinya, kader PKK di tingkat desa dan kelurahan akan menjadi ujung tombak edukasi sekaligus koordinator pengumpulan minyak jelantah dari masyarakat. Program ini juga diperluas melalui jaringan Posyandu yang jumlahnya mencapai 49.149 lembaga di seluruh Jawa Tengah.

“Bukan hanya PKK, nanti kita juga melibatkan Posyandu yang jumlahnya 49.149 lembaga. Ini merupakan potensi yang luar biasa untuk kita bisa membentuk ekonomi sirkular di Jawa Tengah,” beber Nawal.

Ia menjelaskan, konsep ekonomi sirkular menjadi penting karena minyak jelantah tidak lagi dipandang sebagai limbah, melainkan dapat diolah kembali menjadi berbagai produk bernilai ekonomi.

“Bagaimana minyak jelantah ini juga menjadi sumber untuk diolah menjadi biodiesel misalnya, atau bioaftur maupun berbagai produk bernilai ekonomi lainnya,” ungkap Ketua TP Posyandu Jateng tersebut.

Nawal menambahkan, pemanfaatan minyak jelantah juga telah menjadi bagian dari pengembangan Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) di Kilang Pertamina Cilacap.

Ia pun mengapresiasi TP PKK Kabupaten Batang yang lebih dahulu menjalankan program serupa. Sejak Juni 2025, pengelolaan minyak jelantah di daerah tersebut telah menghasilkan omzet sekitar Rp170 juta.

“Ini membuktikan bahwa limbah rumah tangga kini telah menjadi bagian dari transisi, menuju energi yang lebih bersih dan berkelanjutan,” imbuh istri Wakil Gubernur Jateng tersebut.

Sementara itu, Direktur PT BioSirkular Inovasi Indonesia Dicka Dwi Candra mengatakan, program tersebut merupakan tindak lanjut dari nota kesepahaman yang telah ditandatangani bersama TP PKK dan TP Posyandu Jateng pada peringatan Hari Bumi, 22 April 2026 lalu.

Menurutnya, skema program dijalankan melalui empat tahapan utama, yakni edukasi masyarakat, penyediaan titik pengumpulan minyak jelantah di desa dan kelurahan, penjemputan oleh operator di tingkat kecamatan, serta pencatatan digital dan konversi hasil penjualan.

Dicka menjelaskan, setiap satu liter minyak jelantah dihargai Rp7.000. Dari nilai tersebut, Rp5.000 diberikan kepada warga, sedangkan Rp2.000 menjadi pemasukan bagi kas PKK desa.

“Melalui program ini kita harap ekonomi sirkular berbasis rumah tangga akan aktif kembali dan menjadi penggerak untuk pembangunan keberlanjutan,” kata Dicka.

Selain mendorong pengelolaan limbah rumah tangga, kegiatan tersebut juga diisi dengan penandatanganan nota kesepakatan antara TP PKK Jateng dan PT Pegadaian (Persero) Kanwil XI Semarang terkait sinergi program pemberdayaan keluarga melalui gerakan pilah sampah menjadi tabungan emas.

title: Hawaii Becomes Fifth State to Set a Clean Fuel Standard | DRGNews

The new law, which has garnered support from Clean Fuels Alliance America, aims to drive demand and open a new market for biodiesel, renewable diesel, and sustainable aviation fuel, all while spurring economic activity and improving the health of citizens.
The legislation tasks the Hawaii Department of Transportation with developing regulations to reduce transportation emissions by 10% from 2019 levels by 2035, and no less than 50% by 2045.
“As a native of Hawaii, I am thrilled by the state’s leadership in passing the Clean Fuel Standard,” says Cory-Ann Wind, Director of State Regulatory Affairs for Clean Fuels.
“Cleaner fuels like biodiesel, renewable diesel, and sustainable aviation fuel will play a significant role in helping Hawaii reach its climate goals.” Hawaii becomes the fifth state to pass a clean fuel standard, alongside California, Oregon, Washington, and New Mexico.
text:
Hawaii Governor Josh Green signed legislation to create a clean fuel standard for the state.

The new law, which has garnered support from Clean Fuels Alliance America, aims to drive demand and open a new market for biodiesel, renewable diesel, and sustainable aviation fuel, all while spurring economic activity and improving the health of citizens. The legislation tasks the Hawaii Department of Transportation with developing regulations to reduce transportation emissions by 10% from 2019 levels by 2035, and no less than 50% by 2045.

“As a native of Hawaii, I am thrilled by the state’s leadership in passing the Clean Fuel Standard,” says Cory-Ann Wind, Director of State Regulatory Affairs for Clean Fuels. “Cleaner fuels like biodiesel, renewable diesel, and sustainable aviation fuel will play a significant role in helping Hawaii reach its climate goals.”

Hawaii becomes the fifth state to pass a clean fuel standard, alongside California, Oregon, Washington, and New Mexico.

text:
by Kevon Browne

St. Kitts and Nevis (WINN)—Dr Dennis McCall, a Kittitian-born aviation strategist and researcher, was featured on the Eastern Caribbean Central Bank (ECCB) Connects program to discuss how a stronger aviation sector can drive economic transformation through the “Big Push” agenda.

Dr McCall, who holds a PhD in Air Transport Management from De Montfort University, focuses his research on balancing air transport growth with socio-environmental protection, specifically tailored for Small Island Developing States (SIDS).

“So one of the most critical insights is that the Caribbean aviation industry has been facing the same problems for the past 25 years, and we’ve had almost 10 to 12 studies that have been conducted on just travelling in the region from 2000, I think it is up until this year we have 2026, and we’ve been having the same challenges, the exact same challenges. I don’t think that it challenged my initial assumptions, reason being is because I’ve always had a love for the aviation industry since I was in high school so I always used to read a whole lot about what has been happening and the affordability to travel and I realised that it really truly confirmed my assumptions about the aviation industry in the region but what we can say though is that we’ve never been more connected than we are currently. We’re very, very connected even with the collapse of Liat 1974, I think it is, we’re still well connected within the region; however, we still have the same problems existing.”

Bridging the physical gaps between isolated Caribbean nations to ensure the seamless movement of people is essential, yet Dr McCall acknowledges that challenges still persist.

“It’s very hard for us to move between certain countries, so if we were to move from St. Kitts and Nevis to go down to St. Vincent, it’s going to take us a full day or two days, having to even overnight in Antigua or overnight in Barbados, which most passengers have to do and it’s still very, very expensive to travel in the region. One of the other issues that we’ve been faced with is that we have persons working within the aviation industry that don’t necessarily have the aviation experience and the industry is such a unique one where even though you can apply your skills that you’ve learned elsewhere the industry is one that needs specialised training so whether it’s training from Airport Council International or from IATA or from ICAO so those are some of the key problems that we’re having and it really didn’t challenge my assumptions but rather confirmed some of the assumptions that I had before.”

Dr McCall outlines how strategic aviation infrastructure and policy serve as the primary catalyst for regional economic transformation.

The “Big Push” is essentially a coordinated, massive investment across multiple integrated sectors to break out of economic stagnation.

For the Caribbean, Dr McCall argues that aviation shouldn’t be viewed merely as an isolated luxury service, but rather as foundational economic infrastructure.

High airfares, fragmented regional carriers, and inefficient regulatory policies currently act as barriers.

By creating a unified aviation policy, the region can unlock massive economic multipliers across agriculture, tourism, and services.

“The biggest problem that we currently have is the affordability of travel. In the past, a representative from IATA indicated that the Caribbean has the highest travel costs in the entire world, and because we’re a global one of the most popular tourist destinations, we’re kind of taking ourselves out of the market because of that affordability. So our taxes, fees, and charges are extremely high to travel in the region, and if we’re trying to double the economy with this big push agenda, where the lack of ability to afford to travel between St Kitts and Nevis and St Martin or St Kitts and Nevis and St Lucia, we’re kind of undermining our ability to even double the economy. If we really and truly tackle those TFCs I think we’ll be in a better position I know Barbados would have tried to to do so I think it was last year they would have tried to would have come on board as well so we recently had the aviation day in Bahamas or Bermuda it was a few months ago by CTO and they were they’re repeating the same issues about the affordability travel and it needing some serious intervention. I know the Caribbean Development Bank would have just released a report as well about the affordability to travel within the region, so all of these things are still coming up. If we tackle that the TFCs and tackle being able to fly between the islands a little bit more cheaper, I think it would definitely help a whole lot with the big push agenda.”

McCall also suggests less government intervention in any regional airline solution from the OECS.

“One of the things that we really need to look into is having a hands-off approach towards the establishment of this regional airline and we are talking about the hands-off approach from my research would have found that there’s high influence of political interference in there so having a hands-off approach kind of minimises the impact that this political interference would have on the regional airline we don’t want governments to use this airline like a like a school bus like their own personal school bus or their own personal airline it’s not a private it’s not a private airline to be fair so having a hands-off approach establishing an independent body as well to to govern the operations of that entire airline I think it would be fantastic job for them to do.”

Beyond affordability, transitioning to a model of “responsible aviation” to safeguard the environment while supporting the region’s highly tourism-dependent economy, and establishing structured cooperation frameworks to ease cross-border logistics, expand regional air cargo, and attract foreign capital, are paramount to bolstering the region’s economic portfolio.

“They need to make it a little bit more affordable as well in order to travel. I would assume that the OASIS countries would be subsidising the cost of travel between the airlines, as well as the aviation industry has been moving towards net zero by 2050. It’d be really good for us to invest in aircraft that are more sustainably minded. There’s a big push around the world for sustainable aviation fuel, and within the Caribbean, we don’t really have the resources in order to tackle sustainable aviation fuel, but we should use aircraft that are more sustainably minded. I know the ATRs that we normally use for LIAT 20. I think it is into the Caribbean as well, so they’ve actually been doing a lot of research into having a hydrogen-powered aircraft, so we should use some more sustainably minded aircraft. Within the UK and in other European countries as well, the region being having the biggest impact from climate change. This should be a core area for us to look at. Sustainability should be at the heart of the operations of this year of this airline as well, not just from an environmental standpoint, but looking at it from a social and economic standpoint as well too.”

Integrating green policies and decarbonization strategies into local airline and airport operations to ensure long-term climate resilience is also on the agenda, not just through St. Kitts and Nevis’ Sustainable Island State Agenda but also throughout the region.

text:
Lisbon: Portugal is seeking Brazilian investment to establish one or two advanced biofuel and sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) plants as part of a joint initiative aimed at supplying both domestic and European markets, the country’s Energy Minister Maria da Graça Carvalho said.

Carvalho said she would discuss the proposal with her Brazilian counterpart during a visit to Brasília next week, highlighting Brazil’s global leadership in biofuels and Portugal’s strategic location as a gateway to Europe, Reuters reported.

The proposed project aims to combine Brazil’s technological expertise in advanced biofuels and SAF with Portugal’s access to European markets, where demand for low-carbon transport fuels is expected to grow.

“Brazil has been a leader for many years and has significant technological expertise in advanced biofuels and SAF. We want to offer the conditions in Portugal to establish one or two plants to produce these fuels,” Carvalho told reporters.

She said the project, which has the support of Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, could be developed as a joint venture to supply both Portugal and other European countries.

Carvalho added that she would visit biofuel production facilities in Brazil next week. Any investment proposals for similar plants in Portugal would be coordinated through AICEP, the country’s foreign investment promotion agency.

Portugal’s advanced biofuels sector is still at an early stage. Energy company Galp is currently constructing a 270,000-tonne-per-year renewable fuels plant in Sines, which is expected to begin producing sustainable aviation fuel and renewable diesel in 2026.

Carvalho also said Brazil is Portugal’s largest crude oil supplier, accounting for 44% of the country’s oil imports, while Algeria ranks second. Nigeria and the United States are Portugal’s main suppliers of natural gas.

She noted that although Portugal has diversified its energy imports and is not heavily dependent on the Gulf region, it remains exposed to fluctuations in global energy prices.

title: Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Aircraft Propulsion - ePlaneAI
description:

text:
Imagine cruising thousands of feet above the Earth on a long-haul flight. While the experience may seem routine and safe, the aircraft engine powering the journey represents one of the most sophisticated machines ever constructed. Today, these engines are entering a new era—one defined by artificial intelligence (AI). This technology is transforming conventional propulsion systems into intelligent entities capable of learning, adapting, and optimizing performance in real time.

From Conventional Engines to Intelligent Systems

For decades, advancements in aircraft engines centered on enhancing thrust, fuel efficiency, and reliability through engineering innovations and materials science. Despite these improvements, engines remained largely passive, dependent on human oversight and scheduled maintenance protocols. The advent of AI is fundamentally altering this dynamic. Modern engines, outfitted with hundreds of sensors, continuously collect and analyze vast streams of operational data. This capability enables them to detect anomalies, optimize performance, and learn from each flight, marking a significant shift toward truly intelligent aviation systems.

The Role of AI in Engine Operation

Artificial intelligence empowers engines to process immense volumes of data, identify patterns, and make informed decisions autonomously. Parameters such as temperature, pressure, vibration, fuel flow, rotational speed, exhaust gas temperature, and various engine health metrics are constantly monitored. Machine learning algorithms compare real-time sensor data against millions of historical records, allowing engines to detect unusual operating conditions, predict potential failures, recommend corrective actions, and optimize performance throughout the flight. This integration of AI is transforming aircraft engines from purely mechanical devices into adaptive propulsion systems.

Predictive Maintenance and Operational Efficiency

One of the most significant applications of AI in aviation is predictive maintenance. Traditionally, airlines have relied on scheduled maintenance or reactive repairs, approaches that often result in unnecessary part replacements or costly delays. AI enables engines to monitor their own health continuously, using machine learning to predict component wear, identify hidden faults, estimate remaining service life, and schedule maintenance only when necessary. Companies such as GE Aerospace have already implemented AI-powered engine health monitoring across global fleets, yielding reduced operational costs, minimized downtime, and enhanced aircraft availability.

Enhancing Fuel Efficiency and Environmental Sustainability

Fuel consumption remains one of the largest expenses and environmental challenges in aviation. AI contributes to addressing these issues by enabling engines to make intelligent adjustments during every phase of flight. By optimizing fuel-air mixtures, combustion efficiency, and other engine parameters, AI systems help reduce fuel consumption and emissions. This not only lowers operational costs for airlines but also supports broader efforts to achieve greener skies.

Challenges and Market Dynamics

Despite the promising advances, the integration of AI into aircraft propulsion faces considerable challenges. The industry must navigate physical infrastructure limitations and power constraints as it moves beyond initial returns on investment. Market responses have been mixed, with aerospace and technology stocks experiencing volatility amid skepticism regarding the sustainability of AI-related expenditures. Economic pressures and tightening IT budgets have contributed to doubts about the continuation of rapid gains in this sector.

Industry competitors are adopting varied strategies in response. Some emphasize AI’s potential to create new jobs, while others advocate for strategic investments to maintain competitive advantage. As the aerospace sector contends with these economic and operational headwinds, the incorporation of AI into aircraft propulsion remains a transformative development—one that promises smarter, safer, and more efficient flight in the years ahead.
